chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-Ash'ath, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Our Shia are those who exchange gifts in our Wilayah, love one another for our sake, visit one another to revive our affairs; those who, when angry, do not oppress, and when pleased, do not extravagance. They are a blessing upon their neighbors, and a safety for those who mix with them.'
ai.seo_question: What are the key characteristics and social behaviors of the Shia according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking back to Imam Ali (AS) defines the 'Shi'a' not merely by lineage but by active social engagement and ethical moderation. It underscores the concept of 'Wala' (loyalty) as a dynamic force for social cohesion, where mutual visitation and love serve to revive the religious cause, reflecting the Shia ideal of balanced conduct (Wasatiyyah) in both anger and joy.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Amro Bin Al Ash’as, from Abdullah Bin Hammad Al Ansary, from Amro bin Abu Al Miqdam, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Ourasws Shia are reciprocating (gifts etc.) regarding ourasws Wilayah, loving each other regarding ourasws cordiality, visiting each other reviving ourasws matters (Ahadeeth), those when they are angry are not oppressive, and if they are pleased, they are not being extravagant. They are a Blessing upon the ones who are their neighbours, a safety for the ones they are mixing with’.
en.sarwar: 24. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr ibn al- Ash’ath from ‘Abd Allah ibn Hammad al-Ansari from ‘Amr ibn abu al-Miqdam from his father from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) has said, ‘Our Shi’a (followers) spend for (the cause of) our Walayah (Divine Authority), love each other for the sake of our love, and visit each other to preserve our cause. They are those who do not commit injustice when angered, and are not excessive when they agree. They are blessings for the neighbors and peace for those who associate with them.’”
